decisions.basis: The sources support different rules, but limited-benefit coverage and an ordinary denial can both permit savings. Each does not guarantee three distinct outcomes.

decisions.quote: A child may also lose CHIP eligibility if the family keeps the Marketplace plan.
decisions.basis: Captured HealthCare.gov page explicitly says You may no longer qualify for CHIP if you keep your Marketplace plan. The same source describes CHIP as covering children/pregnant women. The article separately explains that parents and children can follow different coverage paths; it does not say parental Marketplace enrollment automatically disqualifies all children.

decisions.quote: HealthCare.gov says to tell the state agency if you want to keep both, and notes that a child may no longer qualify for CHIP if the family keeps the Marketplace plan.
decisions.basis: The source directly says If you want to keep both, tell your state agency followed by the conditional CHIP warning. Preserve may and the official-agency instruction.

decisions.quote: Neither option is the better choice for every household, because eligibility rules decide which coverage comes with financial help.
decisions.basis: The approved brief explicitly excludes a universal winner. HealthCare.gov establishes state/category variation and free or low-cost Medicaid for eligible groups; IRS/HealthCare.gov condition Marketplace savings on income, other coverage and filing/status rules, including limited-benefit and work-denial distinctions. The article then tells eligible readers to obtain an official result, compare actual premiums/provider networks when Marketplace coverage applies, and confirm replacement coverage. This is a supported decision rule, not an evasive purchase verdict, empirical superiority claim or product test.
